**Eval runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-suites` | A
uthor-only: create a suite + its test cases from `name` + `serverIds` + a default `model` + `tests`, WITHOUT running it; responds
`201` + `suiteId`. Each test's case body is an ordered `steps` array (prompt / toolCall / interact / assert); per-test `model`/`pr
ovider`/`runs` are optional and fall back to suite defaults |\n| `POST .../eval-runs` | Create a run from a `suiteId` (rerun; `ser
verIds` optional — defaults to the suite's saved servers) or `suiteName` + inline `tests` + `serverIds` (new suite). `environmentI
d` (requires `suiteId`) runs against one of the suite's attached environments instead. Responds `202` + `runId` |\n| `PATCH .../ev
al-suites/{suiteId}` | Edit suite settings, including `environmentIds` — the project environments the suite runs against (non-empt
y array sets/replaces, `null` clears) |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/schedule` | Enable/disable scheduled runs; `environmen
tId` pins which environment they launch |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` | Run status, result, and summary — poll until terminal.
Carries `gateWaiver`: the audited override in force over this run's gate, or `null` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate` | The st
ored suite quality-gate report for this run (`passed` / `failed` / `non_gateable` / `not_configured`). `not_configured` is a 200 r
eport, never a missing route. A deployment that predates the evaluator answers `422 FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs
/{runId}/decision-summary` | **Start here when a run did not pass.** The canonical run decision contract: the verdict and where it
came from, counts labelled with the population they count, the run's own verdict decision, and per-trial diagnostics with the use
r-value chain, the first failed stage, the failure category, evidence scoped to that stage, and one next action (paginated) |\n| `
POST .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | Override a **failing** run's release gate until `expiresAt` (required, future, max 30 d
ays out), with a `reason` (required, max 500 chars). Manage tier. Does NOT change the run's `result` — the run keeps its verdict a
nd the waiver is reported alongside it. `409` when one is already in force, returning the existing waiver |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/
{runId}/gate-waivers` | The waiver in force over a run, or `null`. Readable by anyone who can view the run |\n| `DELETE .../eval-r
uns/{runId}/gate-waivers/{waiverId}` | Revoke a waiver, putting the gate back. Idempotent — a second call reports the original rev
ocation rather than restamping it |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations` | Per-iteration results: tool calls, token usage, la
tency (paginated) |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations/{iterationId}/trace` | Full trace: messages + expected-vs-actual anal

ysis |
| `GET .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/runs` | Recent runs for a suite, newest first |

**Eval result ingestion** (`/projects/
{projectId}/eval-ingest/...`) — how `@mcpjam/sdk` saves results from eval runs executed outside the platform (local dev, CI). The
`{projectId}` segment accepts the literal `default` for the key org's Default project. Most users never call these directly — set
`MCPJAM_API_KEY` and the [SDK reporter](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/concepts/saving-results.md) does:\n\n| Endpoint | What it does

|
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-ingest/report` | One-shot: create a run from finished results and finalize it |
| `POST .../eval-
ingest/runs/start` | Chunked flow: create (or idempotently reuse) a run by `externalRunId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/iterati
ons` | Append an iteration batch to a started run |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/finalize` | Finalize a chunked run (idempotent)
|\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` | Store one artifact's raw bytes (widget HTML too large to send inline) and return its `stor
ageId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts/upload-url` | Retired. Answers `410 Gone` with `details.code: \"SDK_UPGRADE_REQUIRED\"
`. `@mcpjam/sdk` 8.17.0 and later upload artifacts with `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` instead |\n\n**Agent** (`/projects/{proje

ctId}/agent`) — a headless assistant turn for
building conversational surfaces (the MCPJam Slack app is the first consumer):

|
Endpoint | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `POST .../agent` | Run ONE assistant turn over a `messages` history (`{role: \"user\"\\|\
"assistant\", content}` items, max 50 messages × 8 KB each, 96 KB total). The model is pinned server-side and billed to the projec
t. The turn can read project servers/suites/runs and **create eval suites**; it can NOT start runs — kick those off yourself with
`POST .../eval-runs`. Responds synchronously with `reply`, the `toolCalls` it made, `createdResources` (ids + app links), and toke
n `usage`. Capped at 4 concurrent turns per organization and \\~90 s wall clock. **Not idempotent — never blind-retry**: dedupe on
your own trigger identity, and on an error response check `details.createdResources` (and, after a lost response, list suites) be

fore retrying, or you'll create duplicates |

**Studies** (`/projects/{projectId}/studies...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |\n| `GET .../studies` | List the project's published studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |\n| `GET .
../studies/{studyId}` | One study's full read: model, system prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environment it pu
blishes, and its insights envelope. The last two need workspace membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, never null

|

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Swarms and User Testing are enabled per organization.** Everything in the
> four sections below is behind
that gate, enforced server-side. If it is not\n> on for your organization, the reads generally return empty and every **write**\n
> — creating a persona or goal, launching a run, publishing a study,\n> requesting insights — answers `403` with a message naming

the feature, not a
> `404` and not a validation error.
>
> Five operations are deliberately outside the gate, because every one
of them\n> *reduces* exposure and spend: cancelling a goal run, unpublishing a\n> study, and archiving a persona, goal or swarm (

each one's `DELETE`). An
> organization that loses access can still stop what is running and clean up
> what it authored.
>
>
Ask us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) if you want it turned on.\n\n**Swarms — authoring** (`/projects/{projectId}/per
sonas...`, `.../goals...`,\n`.../swarms...`) — the definitions a swarm run executes. A **persona** is a\nreusable synthetic charac
ter; a **goal** is the task you point one at; a\n**swarm** is an authoring container holding defaults for the goals made\nunder it

. Nothing here starts anything — launching is
`POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs`.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .
../personas` | List the project's personas |\n| `POST .../personas` | Create a persona (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../p
ersonas/{personaId}` | One persona |\n| `PATCH .../personas/{personaId}` | Update a persona. Goals reference it by id, so renaming
is safe |\n| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a persona. **409** while goals still reference it |\n| `GET .../goals` |
List the project's goals |\n| `POST .../goals` | Create a goal (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and `swarmId` must be in t
his project |\n| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |\n| `PATCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null` CLEARS `environmentId
s`; `iterations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |\n| `DELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal — existing runs keep p
ointing at the definition they executed |\n| `GET .../swarms` | List swarm containers |\n| `POST .../swarms` | Create a swarm cont
ainer (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../swarms/{swarmId}` | One swarm |\n| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmId}` | Update the conta
